name: fastapi-request-scoped-serialization-context
instr:
FastAPI cannot provide request-scoped serialization context for audience-aware Pydantic and recursive JSON serialization. Implement it consistently for FastAPI and APIRouter registrations across ordinary responses, server-sent events, errors, and OpenAPI documents. Applications that do not opt in must remain unchanged.

Compose application, router, and route contexts without mutating supplied mappings. Under MERGE, precedence runs from application to router to route. Resolve providers exactly once with the current Request, including asynchronous providers, before nested model serializers observe the winning value. Keep the resolved mapping stable throughout the response and isolated from concurrent and later requests.

Pass context to validation-mode and serialization-mode Pydantic field serializers in nested models while respecting response-model inclusion and exclusion. jsonable_encoder must accept explicit context and propagate it recursively through models, dataclasses, containers, and custom encoders.

Every server-sent event item must use its request's stable context, including nested values across suspension and resumption, without changing metadata or framing. Interleaved streams must retain separate contexts. A first-item serialization failure must emit nothing or contaminate the next request.

Contextual UJSONResponse and ORJSONResponse rendering must raise UnsupportedSerializationContext identifying the consumer before emitting bytes. Context-free rendering remains
